descriptions.text: The exploit was due to a vulnerability in the withdrawWithoutHedge function of a deprecated contract. The _withdraw function, called by withdrawWithoutHedge, calculated the withdrawal amount based on the t.share of the current "tranche." However, the crucial flaw was that t.share was not updated after a withdrawal. Additionally, a state check (require(t.state == TrancheState.Open)) that should have restricted withdrawals to open tranches was commented out. This combination allowed the attacker to repeatedly call withdrawWithoutHedge within a loop, each time withdrawing funds based on the original t.share value, effectively draining the contract.
